exposure: knowledge on labor and delivery (LAD) danger signs
privacy and respect in health institutions
cohort: The study included 707 pregnant women from Southern Ethiopia.
finding: The prevalence of birth preparedness and complication readiness was 30%, with higher odds among women from high economic class, those with ≥4 ANC visits, those who received BP/CR advice, and those knowledgeable on LAD danger signs, while lower odds were found in multiparous women and those from food insecure households.
